summary: Parkevtate Vosianc examines International Paper (IP) after management raised its 2026 macroeconomic headwind estimate from $50 million to $150 million, citing elevated transportation costs, higher corrugated container costs, and increased employee health expenses, with price hikes planned to offset them and better profitability expected in the second half. Revenue has been volatile over the decade ($21B to $17B to $24B TTM), though the North American box transport rate rose 1.7% in H1 despite a declining overall market. He sees tariffs and shrinking disposable income (rent, insurance, healthcare costs) as significant headwinds. Operating margin peaked near 13% in 2019 and fell to just 0.9% TTM, with return on invested capital at -9.6%. Management is implementing turnaround changes, but he remains less confident than the average analyst. At a forward P/E of 11.4 — half the S&P 500 — he still finds it expensive and would prefer a mid-single-digit multiple. His DCF forecasts free cash flow dropping from $840M in 2025 to $360M in 2026 before recovering to $1.3B in 2027, yielding a $43 fair value versus a $34 market price (~26% upside). Call: IP BUY, but with low conviction — he wants at least one quarter of improving performance before getting stronger.
title: International Paper Stock: Buy or Sell in September?
